title: Repo record — /registry/repo/{node_id}.json
description: The published per-repository record: one of the three inputs to the coverage function (`cov-v2`, `cov-v1` before it; FS-10 §4.2) and the data behind the public project page (WEB-080). Published for every registered repository, whether or not its admins have claimed it, in state `registered`, and for `suspended`, `quit` and `delisted` ones (ops decision D82 item 1); a record published before D82 carries `verified` where one published since carries `registered`. *(Amended 2026-09-30, D82 and its dated note (d) of 2026-09-29: it said "Published for repositories in state `verified`, `suspended`, `quit` or `delisted`; `detected` repositories appear in aggregate counts only (FS02-062, GH-014).")* A delisted or quit repository still HAS a record and still computes coverage — entitlements and vesting stand (D12) — and `state` is what the answer reports as `basis.repoState` (FS-10 §4.3 step 1), cov-v2 reporting a `verified` record as `registered`. A repository with no record is answered only for an organisation holding a Pass inside its term, with `basis.repoState` `no-record` (cov-v2; ops decisions D48 item 5 and D82 item 10). At P-M2 the `stats` block is deliberately ABSENT: Purpose-Points and charity figures do not exist before the first disbursed ledger row, and publishing a zero would be theatre (VS-18, NEV-017).

generatedAt.description: When this artifact was rendered. Also served as `Last-Modified` (FS10-003). Regeneration is eventually consistent by design — nothing may promise real time (FS-00 §7.5).

source.description: Which plane produced this artifact. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders such an artifact is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it (FS-10 §2 v0 note; the edge route answers `sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). `registry-v0` is the P-M2 production source of record — the curated registry repository the index is built from. `platform` is the P-M3 producer of record — the platform database, rendered by `jobs.index-build`. Optional, and its absence asserts nothing: an artifact whose body cannot carry the label borrows the plane's declaration from `/registry/index/meta.json`. The enum widens additively when the P-M3 producer takes a value of its own, and `platform` (2026-09-12) is that widening: `jobs.index-build` writes it in `PSN_ENV=prod` and writes `fixture` in every other environment, so a reader can still tell a production plane from a synthetic one by the label alone.

orgId.description: Owner node_id — an organisation's `O_…` or a user account's `U_…`, taken from the curated record's `owner_node_id` (ops decision D42). THIS is what a Portfolio-lane entitlement's `scope.org` is compared against (FS-10 §4.3 step 5c) — a transfer changes portfolio matching from the next publish, never the repository key. Absent when the registry records none, and then no Portfolio term matches the repository. Discovery records it for every repository it confirms since 2026-09-29 (PS-1183: the owner looked up once per scan in the current id form); a repository registered before that, or confirmed while GitHub answered only the legacy form, gets it from an `owner-recorded` event (migration 0061, PS-1184), which fills a missing id and never moves a recorded one; a change of owner stays a transfer (FS02-022).

name.description: Display cache only. First character is the registry index shard key (FS02-062).

stateChangedAt.description: The instant the repository's PUBLISHED `state` last changed. From ops decision D82 on, the platform's internal move from `detected` to `verified`, which is a claim, is not a change of published state, since both publish as `registered`: it never sets this instant, and a `registered` record carries the instant the repository became registered, or last returned to `registered`, never the instant its admins claimed it (D82 item 3). A record published before D82, whose published state was `verified`, may carry the instant of the claim. *(Worded 2026-09-30, D82; the member had no description.)*

stateNote.description: The public reason CLASS for a `suspended`, `quit` or `delisted` state — the neutral, published category the tombstone page prints (WEB-075). A CLASS, never a narrative: no account of events, no allegation, no person's name and no third party's, because a registry tombstone is read for years and a sentence written on a bad day is read the same way. Absent when the state has no published reason, which is not the same as a reason nobody may see.

weightClass.description: Pricing weight class as of publication (D11). Never applied retroactively to a purchased term (FS02-016, D12). `utility` (1.7.0; D103 item 2, FS02-073; platform migration 0079): set only by the steward's recorded line count of a registered release, under 5,000 library lines; a Project of such a repository is priced at its band's Utility row.

allocationFrozen.description: Orthogonal flag: allocation skips this repository while true (FS-02 F2). Never changes `state`.

publishedAt.description: Publication date of the licence version this repository carries — the conversion-clock anchor (D9).

apacheConversionDate.description: The fixed date this version becomes plain Apache-2.0: publication + 4 years, guaranteed by the licence text itself (D9). Rendered on the project page (WEB-080).

textSha256.description: SHA-256 of the committed licence text (GH-015 canonical-text evidence).

manifest.description: PURPOSE.yml status. `present: false` renders as 'defaults apply — no manifest, none needed' (FS01-046, VS-18): the manifest is optional and its absence is not a deficiency (D23).

rejections.description: Published rejection records (FS02-052). A non-attribution field carries `path`; the attribution section fails closed as a whole and is reported as one record with `path: "attribution"`.

code.description: Machine code, lowercase snake_case (P-M2 §3.9 casing law) — e.g. `reg.manifest_out_of_bounds`, `reg.manifest_unknown_category`.

given.description: The rejected value, as given. Any JSON type.

bound.description: The published bound that rejected it.

waivers.description: Pointer to the waiver artifact for this repository. At P-M2 `count` is 0 for every repository and the project page renders the honest empty state — waivers require the claim flow (D14, VS-18).

url.description: The shields.io endpoint URL, pinned verbatim to the canonical host in every embed snippet (CERT-027, WEB-084).

state.description: Which badge form this repository's state produces. `registered` for every repository whose `state` is `registered`: every registered repository that is not suspended, whether or not its admins have claimed it (ops decision D82 item 5). `suspended`, `quit` and `delisted` all render neutral, as before — a stale badge never keeps asserting registration (WEB-085).

impactCategoryDefaults.description: The project's own default public-benefit categories (FS02-050 tier 3), in the project's stated order. Absent means the board's published allocation key applies (equal shares to all active recipients while none is published; the word “steward default” is retired, ops decision D117) — a project that chose nothing is not a project that chose none. *(Renamed 2026-09-08, pre-release: the member was `allocationDefaults`, which is the name no other contract uses; `registry-v0-record.v1` 1.1.0 already validates `impact_category_defaults` and the curated registry records carry it, so one vocabulary now spans the record and the artifact built from it. Its items were `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` with `maxItems: 8`; the menu is a closed set of seven, so an open pattern admitted a slug no allocation surface could render. Superseded, kept as history: `allocationDefaults`, an eight-item open-pattern array.)* *(1.5.0, 2026-10-08: derived from `designation` when one is in force — its category slugs with a share above 0, largest share first, ties in the menu's order (the statutes' order of `category-menu.v1`: health, education, poverty-relief, humanitarian-aid, environment, animal-welfare, research) — and kept for readers of the slug list; `designation` is the full statement, with the shares and the share left to the Association. A producer from 1.5.0 on publishes it whenever it publishes `designation`, and publishes `[]` when the designation leaves everything to the Association.)*

designation.description: The project's own designation (statutes Art. 8(4); Calculation Rules Nr. 25), as its administrators saved it, in force for the record's month: the UTC calendar month of `generatedAt` (its first seven characters). In force means the newest of the repository's saved versions whose first month is at or before the record's month. Published per repository and without a floor, because it is the project's statement and names nobody: no administrator, account, version or instant is published (ops decisions D117 and D121 item 1). Its `categories` and `association` are whole percents that make exactly 100, which the producer guarantees and its tests hold it to (JSON Schema cannot state a sum); a category at 0 is not a member. A designation is advisory (Art. 8(4)): it is recorded, published and honoured under the published allocation rule as far as the Association's duties allow, and never binds it; a project's designation routes its repository's money from the market start (Nr. 26). Absent means no designation is in force for the month: the board's published allocation key applies, as for `impactCategoryDefaults`. The contributors' designations are never published here per person; their summary is `contributorDesignations`. *(Added 1.5.0, 2026-10-08, D117 §6.)*

effectiveFrom.description: `YYYY-MM`: the first month of the unbroken run of months, ending with the record's month, in which the designation in force for this repository had exactly these shares. It is ordinarily the month the version in force took effect — the month after it was saved, in Europe/Zurich (D117; platform migration 0077) — and earlier only when that version restated the shares already in force before it, as when a change saved in one month was undone in the same month and never took effect. So every month from `effectiveFrom` through the record's month had this designation in force, and the month before it had another or none. Never later than the record's month.

categories.description: Category slug → whole percent, 1 to 100. A category at 0 is not a member. Empty when the whole designation is left to the Association.

association.description: The whole percent expressly left to the Association ("All"), which the board's published allocation key distributes (Art. 8(4)). 0 when the categories take everything.

contributorDesignations.description:
The contributors' designations for this repository, in summary only (statutes Art. 8(4): recorded and published in summary; Calculation Rules Nr. 26: from the first day): how many contributors have a designation in force for the record's month — the UTC calendar month of `generatedAt` — and the mean share each category and the Association receive across all of them. Contributors' designations: advisory; routes money only after the fairness review (D27). They route no money until a quarter's data and the board's published fairness and abuse review (Nr. 26); until then the project's own designation applies to their part, and without one the board's published allocation key (Nr. 29).

THE FLOOR. Present only when at least 5 contributors have a designation for this repository in force for the record's month (N = 5, ops decision D121 item 1). Below that it is absent, and those contributors' designations are counted only in the registry-wide monthly summary (`designations-summary.v1`, at `/designations/{YYYY-MM}.json`) and shown there only when at least 5 people stand behind what the repository summaries do not show, so that no one person's choice can be read off a small project. Absent therefore says nothing about whether anybody designated. Nothing here names a person: no contributor, account, node id, version or instant is published, and no member can carry one.

WHAT COUNTS. In force for the month, per contributor: the newest of their saved versions for this repository whose first month is at or before the record's month, so each designator holds exactly one designation here, its lines whole percents making 100. A designation whose holder's account was erased stays in force under the pseudonym that replaced their node id (FS03-061) and counts as one designator.

THE MEANS AND THEIR ROUNDING. Each value is the sum of the designators' shares for that member divided by `designators` — a designator with no line for it counts 0 — rounded to one decimal, halves rounded up. In integers, with T the sum of whole percents and n = `designators`: tenths = floor((20 × T + n) / (2 × n)), and the value is tenths / 10. A category is a member when at least one designator gave it a share above 0, so a member reads 0.0 when its mean is below 0.05; `association` is always present and reads 0.0 when nobody left anything to the Association. The exact means sum to 100 and each value differs from its exact mean by at most 0.05, so the members together make 100 within rounding: within 100 ± 0.05 × (the number of members), at most ± 0.4. *(Added 1.6.0, 2026-10-08, D117 §6 and D121 item 1.)*

designators.description: The number of contributors with a designation for this repository in force for the record's month: one per holder, a holder being a node id or the pseudonym an erasure left in its place (FS03-061), so a person whose account was erased and who came back under the same identity is two holders. Never fewer than the floor of 5 (D121 item 1), because below it this object is absent.

categories.description: Category slug → the mean percent across all `designators`, one decimal, rounded as this object's description says. A category no designator gave a share is not a member.

association.description: The mean percent across all `designators` expressly left to the Association ("All"), which the board's published allocation key distributes (Art. 8(4)), one decimal, rounded as this object's description says; 0.0 when nobody left anything to it.

display.description: Optional display metadata echoed from PURPOSE.yml `display` (repository content — escaped, never trusted).

stats.description: P-M3+ ONLY. Absent at P-M2 by design: no Purpose-Points figures, no charity figures, no zero-CHF theatre before the first disbursed ledger row (VS-18, NEV-017, D21). Every money figure that ever appears here is ledger-derived and deep-linked.

coverageCount.description: Number of organisations currently answering yes for this repository.

unclaimedSharePpm.description: Unclaimed share, aggregate only — never per person (D15).

ledgerUrl.description: Deep link to the ledger rows the figure comes from. A figure without its rows is a defect (ENG-043).

categorySlug.description: The seven published categories of the statutes' Art. 7 (D33 item 1). A copy of `category-menu.v1.json#/$defs/slug`, asserted identical to it by the publishing repository's gate — schemas here are self-contained, so one downloaded file validates on its own and cross-file references do not exist.

repoState.description: Published states. `registered` is the one state a record published from ops decision D82 on shows for a repository registered under the network's rules and not suspended, whether or not its admins have claimed it: both of the platform's internal states `detected` and `verified` publish as `registered` (D82 item 1 and its dated note (d) of 2026-09-29). A suspended repository is registered in D82 item 1's sense too, and its record shows `suspended`, as before. `verified` is the state records published before D82 carried for a claimed repository and stays valid for them (versioning policy 4); a producer writes `registered` in its place from D82 on. `suspended`, `quit` and `delisted` are unchanged. The internal state `detected` never appears. *(Amended 2026-09-30: it said "Published subset of the FS-02 §3 enum: `detected` repositories get no record (GH-014).")*

meanPercent.description: A mean percent with one decimal (`contributorDesignations`): a sum of whole percents divided by the number of designators, rounded to one decimal, halves rounded up. JSON Schema cannot hold a number to one decimal without floating-point error, so the producer guarantees it and its tests hold it to it.

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id, in either of the two forms GitHub has issued: the opaque current form (a repository's is `R_`-prefixed) and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository` and whose `=` padding the first alternative cannot express. Widened 2026-09-08 to admit the second: `registry-v0-record.v1` accepts both, so a record the curated registry accepts is publishable in this artifact. The primary key for repositories and people throughout this contract set (FS-00 §6.1).
